title: Bounded-Overlap Shard Rebalancer
prompt:
Implement `rebalance_shards(limit, shards) -> list[str]`. Each shard is an `"id:start:end"` string representing the inclusive integer interval `[start, end]`; IDs are distinct and contain no colon. `limit` is positive.

First process shards in increasing `(start, end, id)` order. For each shard, move its start to the first key at or after its original start whose current coverage is below `limit`. If no such key is within the shard's original interval, discard that shard. Otherwise keep it with its adjusted start and original end; it contributes one unit of coverage on that adjusted closed interval.

After all adjustments, make the kept union gap-free from the smallest original start through the largest original end. Whenever there is a gap, extend the most recently kept shard far enough to close it; if a tail remains after the last kept shard, extend that last shard to the original maximum end. A retained shard can therefore end later than it originally did.

Return retained strings in their processing order. An empty input returns `[]`. The post-adjustment coverage limit applies before this final gap-closing step. Target `O(n log n)` time and `O(n)` auxiliary space; key coordinates can be as large as one billion in magnitude, so do not iterate individual keys.

example.reasoning: The first free key for C is 56; the retained C range is later extended to bridge the gap before D.
